## ReferenceRegistry type

What a reference value type needs to know about every resource a reference can name, keyed by manifest resource key.

**Signature:**

```typescript
type ReferenceRegistry = Readonly<
  Record<
    string,
    {
      readonly id?: ValueType<unknown>
      readonly get?: OperationId
      readonly list?: OperationId
      readonly parents?: ResourceParents
    }
  >
>
```

**References:** [ValueType](./contracts.valuetype.md)<!-- -->, [OperationId](./contracts.operationid.md)<!-- -->, [ResourceParents](./contracts.resourceparents.md)

## Remarks

Each entry carries the resource's identifier value type, when the resource has an identifier; it encodes and decodes the `id` of identity references to that resource. A resource without an identifier (`id` absent) can be referenced only by selector forms: name, index, every, or range. A reference's containers usually belong to other resources, so the table covers every resource of the app that a reference can name, not only the one a position declares. A reference to a resource absent from the table is rejected.

Each entry also names the operations that resolve references to the resource, where it has them: `get` resolves a single-object reference and `list` a collection. Every resolvable object needs its resolving operation (`get` for a single object, a container, and an identity-collection entry; `list` for a collection), because a reference that names a resource without it could never be resolved. Reference value types enforce this in their wire schema, so every boundary applies it.

An entry names its `parents` when an operation resolving references to the resource finds objects only within an object of another resource, by that object's identifier ([ResourceParents](./contracts.resourceparents.md)<!-- -->). A reference resolved through such an operation must carry, as its container, an identity reference to that parent, which is itself resolvable; one without it could never be resolved.

An app contract's `resources` table is assignable to this type; reference value types read it through the [ReferenceScope](./contracts.referencescope.md)<!-- -->.
